title: Deliver the agent-first Fluxgrade SaaS
description: Build Fluxgrade as an agent-first software mission platform. The primary player interface is a real local repository plus the player's normal agent. Fluxgrade provisions isolated running systems, delivers stateful events, accepts deployments through a credential-brokering gateway, performs separate hidden evaluation, records provenance-aware evidence, and emits replayable results. Preserve the static browser game as the trailer. Support public practice, Fluxgrade-hosted private assessments, customer-VPC runtimes, and eventually full private deployment. Completion requires real end-to-end proof, not just code or passing unit tests.

title: Freeze current trailer behavior
description: Protect the existing GitHub Pages trailer before restructuring. Add regression coverage for the title screen, first mission screen, optimal result path, and mobile behavior. Keep existing root URLs and static asset paths working. Acceptance: npm test, npm run test:e2e, and a dedicated trailer regression command all pass against the actual served artifact.
notes: Reality check 2026-08-01: actual trailer code remains the only product runtime; local served artifact passed landing, mission, optimal result, and mobile regression; npm unit and existing E2E gates passed; deployed GitHub Pages title and simulation labeling remain accurate; no SaaS, hosted runtime, or private capability claim added.
close_reason: Verified npm test (5/5), npm run test:e2e, and npm run test:trailer against the spawned served artifact; dedicated regression covers landing/title, first mission, optimal 100-point result, and mobile panels.

title: Introduce workspace tooling without moving the trailer
description: Add pnpm workspaces, shared TypeScript configuration, Vitest workspace configuration, pinned Node version, and root build/test/check scripts. Keep the existing trailer files in place during this task so GitHub Pages is not disrupted. Acceptance: fresh install succeeds, workspace commands run, and every frozen trailer test remains green.
notes: Phase 0 reality check 2026-08-01: actual code now has only foundation tooling plus the static trailer. In a clean temporary directory containing only package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, and pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile exited 0 and installed 50 packages with pnpm 10.33.2. pnpm check exited 0 and exercised strict config loading, unit tests, E2E, and trailer regression; npm test and npm run test:e2e also exited 0. Deployed site remains the accurately labeled deterministic simulation; no agent-first runtime or SaaS capability exists yet.
close_reason: Verified clean-temp pnpm install --frozen-lockfile (exit 0, lockfile current); pnpm check; npm test (5/5); npm run test:e2e. Workspaces, TypeScript base, Vitest projects, exact toolchain pins, lockfile, and aggregate scripts are operational without moving trailer assets.

title: Define and validate the versioned mission package schema
description: Create @fluxgrade/mission-schema using Zod plus YAML loading and JSON Schema export. Require schema version, mission ID/version, candidate artifact digest, runtime image digests, evaluator digest, policies, events, objectives, and limits. Reject unknown schema versions, mutable image tags, missing evaluator digests, duplicate event IDs, and invalid trigger graphs. Include valid and invalid fixtures with unit tests.
notes: Reality check 2026-08-01: implemented @fluxgrade/mission-schema with strict versioned manifests, YAML parse/error/size/node/depth/alias bounds, candidate SHA-256 artifact digest, fully qualified OCI digest pins, strict policies/objectives/limits, duplicate and acyclic event graph checks, and executable draft-2020-12 JSON Schema with parser-only invariants documented. Proof: package unit tests 15/15; package TypeScript build passes; built dist loads checkout-latency@1.0.0, Ajv accepts it, missing-evaluator fixture is rejected, and Ajv rejects traversal paths; pnpm check passes; required npm test (5/5) and npm run test:e2e pass; final independent review APPROVE. No runtime execution, evaluator implementation, signing, hosting, or private capability claimed.
close_reason: Verified strict versioned mission schema, bounded YAML loader, digest-pinned artifacts/images, event DAG validation, authoring JSON Schema through Ajv, valid/invalid fixtures, 15/15 unit tests, built-package smoke, full pnpm check, and preserved trailer gates.

title: Define provenance-aware append-only evidence events
description: Create @fluxgrade/evidence-schema. Event envelopes must identify session, sequence, source, source instance, kind, timestamps, payload digest, previous event digest, event digest, visibility, and retention class. Implement deterministic canonical JSON, SHA-256 hash chaining, append, and verification. Tests must catch payload alteration, provenance changes, sequence gaps, and invalid chains.
notes: Reality check 2026-08-01: implemented @fluxgrade/evidence-schema with strict versioned envelopes, canonical descriptor snapshots, SHA-256 payload/event digests, append and verification, bounded hostile-input handling, and a portable fixture. Proof: package unit tests 18/18; package TypeScript build passes; built dist verifies fixture head 1bf093a2cd753faff2c4dbb676e772d4ca2f69e691f2045688490a465599b9e0 and appends sequence 3 with a valid extended head; pnpm check passes; required npm test (5/5) and npm run test:e2e pass; final independent review APPROVE. No signatures, storage, hosted runtime, or private evaluator claimed.
close_reason: Verified strict provenance-aware evidence envelopes, deterministic canonical JSON and SHA-256 chaining, append/full verification, stable portable fixture, hostile-input defenses, 18/18 unit tests, built-package smoke, full pnpm check, and preserved npm trailer gates.

title: Define the provider-neutral runtime contract and conformance suite
description: Create @fluxgrade/runtime-provider with lifecycle operations for prepare, create, health, readService, submitArtifact, deploy, checkpoint, evaluate, and destroy. Specify idempotency, capability discovery, lifecycle state, and typed failure modes. Build a reusable conformance suite and in-memory fake so mission-engine code cannot depend on Docker or one sandbox vendor.
notes: Reality check 2026-08-01: implemented @fluxgrade/runtime-provider with provider-neutral prepare/create/health/readService/submitArtifact/deploy/checkpoint/evaluate/destroy contract; content-addressed payload verification; scoped idempotency and conflicts; typed failures; full-profile reusable conformance with identity, provenance, isolation, teardown, late-retry, malformed-input, timeout, and cleanup checks; and resettable in-memory test fake. Proof: package build passes; 9/9 package tests pass including nonconforming teardown/identity rejection; built dist lifecycle smoke produced ready -> running -> score 100 -> destroyed and post-destroy invalid-state; full pnpm check passes; mandatory npm test 5/5 and npm run test:e2e pass; independent final contract review APPROVE. Prepare is explicitly non-owning and conformance timeout diagnostic; no Docker, hosted runtime, evaluator, or private capability claimed.
close_reason: Verified provider-neutral runtime contract and reusable full-profile conformance suite end to end.

title: Build the checkout-latency candidate repository
description: Create the first public mission candidate repository. It must be a realistic unfamiliar checkout service with a stale design document, seeded p95 latency regression, saved-payment-method skew, and several attractive wrong fixes. The causal defect is synchronous fraud enrichment introduced by a refactor. Public tests expose the SLO but not hidden invariants. Prove both naive failure modes and a valid causal fix before resetting and digesting the seed.
notes: Reality check 2026-08-01: created the checkout-latency candidate seed and versioned mission manifest. Seed contains a checkout HTTP service, deterministic load generator, synchronous fraud-enrichment regression (card p95 245 ms; saved and aggregate p95 385 ms vs 250 ms SLO), saved-method skew, candidate handoff/AGENTS guidance, and a stale design note that falsely points at payments/retries. External authoring calibration proves fraud bypass meets latency with zero fraud evaluations, blind hedging meets latency with 100 duplicate authorizations, and causal parallelization meets all latency, exactly-once, allow, deny, and release invariants. Proof: 9/9 authoring tests and TypeScript build pass; candidate public test intentionally fails with observed 385 > 250; deterministic packer rebuilds repository.tar.zst byte-for-byte; sha256 f393e315de6db5e39f339c5d6990c6391c79ab72364302ffc27a05193f63c32f matches mission.yaml; clean extracted archive npm ci/build pass, materializes README/AGENTS, health returns 200 ready, saved checkout returns 200 with duration 385; full pnpm check passes 51 Vitest + 5 trailer unit + E2E/trailer; final independent slow review APPROVE. No runtime, evaluator, deployment, or hosted capability claimed.
close_reason: Verified deterministic checkout-latency candidate seed, calibration variants, and content-addressed standalone archive.

title: Build the stateful checkout-latency runtime
description: Create the supporting runtime outside the candidate repository: session gateway, fraud provider, payment ledger, deterministic seed data, health endpoints, and machine-readable metrics. Tests must prove seeded latency, saved-method skew, idempotency behavior, and ledger consistency. The runtime must be deterministic enough for replay and variant calibration.

title: Build the isolated hidden evaluator
description: Create an evaluator container that has no writable candidate-source access and runs outside the candidate process namespace. Emit versioned structured JSON. Hidden checks must cover duplicate authorization holds, active fraud decisions, saved-method success, bounded retries, p95 target, and behavior under provider degradation. Known-good and multiple known-bad artifacts must be classified correctly.

title: Implement stateful midstream mission events
description: Implement the provider-degradation event graph. Deliver exactly once after the first candidate deployment that improves p95, with a deadline fallback if no qualifying deployment occurs. Produce signed machine-readable and human-readable forms, change runtime behavior without revealing the fix, and make event selection deterministic under replay.

title: Implement fluxgrade start and the local Docker provider
description: Create the CLI start command and local Docker RuntimeProvider. Validate the mission package, create a unique workspace, materialize candidate files, initialize Git, write an ignored .env at mode 0600, and acquire a runtime lease. Candidate access must flow through the session gateway rather than provider credentials. The Docker provider must pass the shared conformance suite.

title: Implement the durable local sidecar and repository inbox
description: Build a resumable local sidecar with lock file, acknowledged JSONL spool, atomic inbox writes, and reconnect behavior. Deliver signed events to .fluxgrade/inbox and appropriate human-readable incident updates to incidents/updates. Add terminal and OS notification adapters that fail safely. Kill/restart tests must prove no loss or duplication.

title: Implement agent-friendly status, events, inspect, and check commands
description: Expose concise human output and stable --json output for mission status, event listing, environment inspection, and public checks. Never print tokens or provider credentials. Use meaningful nonzero exit codes for unhealthy, denied, and expired sessions. Snapshot and schema tests must cover all outputs.

title: Implement deployment through a content-addressed artifact boundary
description: Implement fluxgrade deploy without exposing Docker or cloud credentials. Package only the allowed repository root as a content-addressed Git bundle or archive, reject escaped symlinks, ignored secrets, unrelated dirty paths, oversized artifacts, and mutable bases, then build cleanly and deploy to a simulated canary. Emit authoritative deployment and health events.

title: Expose the CLI application services through an optional MCP adapter
description: Create a stdio MCP server for status, events, inspect, check, deploy, and submit. It must delegate to the same application services as the CLI, return structured data plus concise summaries, and remain optional. Document verified integration for Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and generic MCP clients.

title: Freeze and evaluate final mission submissions
description: Implement fluxgrade submit. Require INCIDENT_REPORT.md sections for outcome, evidence, tradeoffs, and residual risk. Freeze the repository digest and evidence-chain head, rebuild from a clean image, execute the hidden evaluator in its separate boundary, enforce idempotency, and prevent later deployments from mutating the submitted result.

title: Generate provenance-aware result reports
description: Create a shared report model and render versioned JSON plus Markdown. Include mission/policy/evaluator versions, final repository digest, authoritative runtime/evaluator evidence, client-observed evidence labeled as such, timeline, verification strengths, integrity gaps, and known limitations. Golden tests must verify stable output and secret/path redaction.

title: Implement deterministic mission replay
description: Build a pure reducer over the append-only event stream and artifacts. Reject shuffled or invalid chains. Render a terminal replay of deployments, requirement updates, system consequences, and evaluation without depending on the original conversation. Fixed fixtures must produce byte-stable output after the runtime has been destroyed.

title: Add adversarial boundary and recovery tests
description: Create adversarial and end-to-end tests for escaped submission symlinks, accidental .env staging, evaluator access attempts, duplicate deploys, sidecar interruption, runtime restart, disconnected event delivery, expired sessions, and naive fixes that improve one metric while violating payment invariants. Fix only demonstrated failures and require detailed logs.

title: Run and document three real-agent playthroughs
description: Complete the mission end to end with Hermes without a Fluxgrade skill, Claude Code or Codex using only AGENTS.md, and a human using CLI without MCP. Record observed friction, event delivery, unsupported claims, deployment usability, report trust, and rematch intent. Gate cloud work on reliable browser-free completion and evaluator discrimination.

title: Run a measured managed-runtime bakeoff
description: Apply the same RuntimeProvider conformance suite to E2B, Daytona, and one AWS-native baseline. Measure lifecycle, endpoint exposure, egress defaults, metadata blocking, isolation, resource exhaustion, TTL, artifact export, regions/private options, teardown, and real cost per completed mission. Reject any provider that cannot enforce minimum policy and document replacement exit criteria.

title: Implement the selected hosted runtime provider
description: Map the selected managed sandbox to RuntimeProvider without changing mission-engine code. Provider credentials stay only in the control-plane worker. The local client receives session-scoped gateway capabilities. Prove a complete remote checkout mission, destroy the runtime, and independently verify no active resource remains.

title: Implement the minimal hosted session API and gateway
description: Create durable API and worker services for invitation token claim, session leases, scoped/expiring/revocable tokens, artifact upload, deployment requests, event ingest, and teardown. Persist projections in PostgreSQL and content-addressed artifacts in S3-compatible storage. Tests must cover idempotency, redaction, rate limits, reconnect, and full completion from a machine without Docker.

title: Implement organizations, memberships, and tenant authorization
description: Add organizations, users, memberships, roles, and least-privilege authorization to the control plane. Every tenant-owned record must carry organization identity. High-risk access must be enforced at application and database policy layers. Include cross-tenant denial tests and audit events.

title: Implement private mission libraries and immutable releases
description: Add employer-private mission libraries, authoring/review lifecycle, immutable version release, signed manifests, sealed variants, retirement, and private OCI storage. Candidate bundles must exclude hidden evaluator source. Publicly released missions can never later be represented as sealed hiring variants.

title: Implement employer invitations and candidate consent
description: Add invitation creation, expiration, cancellation, reassignment, policy disclosure, candidate consent, accommodations, and session claim. Preserve candidate privacy and accessibility. Tests must cover unauthorized claim, reuse, revocation, and policy-version pinning.

title: Implement reviewer reports, disagreement, and appeals
description: Add role-specific reviewer reports, structured rubric review, reviewer disagreement capture, candidate-visible result boundaries, correction, appeal, and audit history. Do not make validated hiring claims until calibration evidence supports them.

title: Implement billing entitlements and usage metering
description: Add subscription, entitlement, metering, invoice projection, pilot credits, and denial-of-wallet controls behind an adapter. Runtime session creation must respect entitlements and budgets without coupling core assessment logic directly to Stripe.

title: Implement public accounts, seasons, ratings, and rematches
description: Add public identities, mission history, disclosed fairness divisions, seasons, rivals, ratings, replays, and immediate rematches. Do not merge Open Stack and standardized results into a misleading universal rank. Rating updates must be versioned and replayable.

title: Implement signed result credentials and public verification
description: Sign result manifests with asymmetric KMS-backed keys, publish a minimal verification endpoint, support key rotation and revocation, and make every credential identify mission, variant, runtime, policy, evaluator, scoring version, final digest, and integrity limitations.

title: Implement enterprise identity, retention, and residency controls
description: Add OIDC/SAML, SCIM, employer-defined evidence retention, deletion/export, regional placement, customer-managed key hooks, support audit tooling, backup/restore drills, and policy tests. Keep external providers behind adapters so full private deployment remains possible.

title: Deliver and prove the customer-VPC data plane runner
description: Deploy an outbound-only mTLS runner by Terraform into a fresh customer AWS account. Use customer ECR, S3, KMS, logs, VPC, and runtime placement. Prove no candidate/evaluator payload reaches SaaS when forbidden, only approved result projections leave, teardown and key revocation are customer-controlled, and install/upgrade/rollback/uninstall all work.

title: Deliver a fully private deployment for a committed design partner
description: Package portal, API, workers, database dependencies, object storage integration, signing, identity, mission registry, runner, telemetry, backup, upgrade, and offline license support using signed images plus Terraform/Helm. Execute only for a committed design partner. Verify disconnected operation, customer-controlled retention, rollback, restore, and complete uninstall.

title: Build challenge calibration and validity pipeline
description: Create a calibration and validity pipeline before private hiring claims. Measure variant equivalence, evaluator discrimination, reviewer consistency, candidate outcome distribution, prompt/tool/runtime policy effects, adverse impact, manager usefulness, false-positive/false-negative cases, and cost. Encode pilot kill criteria and release gates. Use frozen fixtures, known-good and known-bad artifacts, blind duplicate review, seeded variants, and versioned datasets. Private mission releases and hiring reports must disclose evidence quality and cannot be promoted beyond experimental until thresholds are met.

title: Publish recovered origins, architecture, Beads plan, and reality check
description: Publish the recovered primary-source Fluxgrade product origins, agent-first SaaS/private-deployment architecture, granular implementation plan, repository-local workflow instructions, reality-check gap analysis, and portable Beads graph. Acceptance: documentation contains no secrets or personal absolute paths; Markdown structure validates; existing unit and deployed E2E tests pass; br graph has no cycles; bvr robot analysis succeeds; commit is pushed and remote branch is verified. Do not include the raw untracked brainstorm transcript in the public commit.
close_reason: Published and verified: origins, architecture, implementation plan, AGENTS workflow, reality check, and portable Beads graph; npm test passed 5/5; npm run test:e2e passed; Markdown and git diff checks passed; gitleaks found no leaks; br reported no cycles; bvr robot triage/insights/plan/next succeeded; pushed main and verified remote commit 31fa137.
